Use this sheet with [the exercise](exercise-student.html). Predict before reading the results, then explain in words. These figures use exact updating or supplied fits, with no new Stan inference.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/functions.R"))
source(here("R/course_data.R"))
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
source(here("R/course_visuals.R"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.width=8,fig.height=4.5)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=14))
```

## More seedlings, same observed proportion

These are the two outcomes of the participant calculation. Both plots use the
same prior, equally spaced grid and axes. Predict the change before viewing the
second figure.

```{r comparisons, fig.height=3.4}
p <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 501)
for (N in c(5, 100)) {
  y <- if (N == 5) 2 else 40
  prior <- dbeta(p, shape1 = 1, shape2 = 1)
  likelihood <- dbinom(x = y, size = N, prob = p)
  posterior <- prior * likelihood
  posterior <- posterior / sum(posterior)
  figure <- tibble(p = p, posterior = posterior) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = p, y = posterior)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, colour = "#d95f02") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 0.02)) +
    labs(x = "Survival probability p",
         y = "Posterior probability per grid point",
         title = paste(y, "survivors out of", N, "seedlings"))
  print(figure)
}
```

Both observed proportions are 0.4. Under this model and prior, the larger survey
gives a narrower posterior: less uncertainty about the survival probability.
The continuous posteriors approximated here are Beta(3,4) and Beta(41,61).
Their means are close, but not identical.

## Optional: a different prior with the same 2/5 data

```{r prior-comparison, fig.height=3.4}
y <- 2
N <- 5
prior <- dbeta(p, shape1 = 8, shape2 = 2)
likelihood <- dbinom(x = y, size = N, prob = p)
posterior <- prior * likelihood
posterior <- posterior / sum(posterior)
tibble(p = p, posterior = posterior) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = p, y = posterior)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, colour = "#d95f02") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 0.02)) +
  labs(x = "Survival probability p",
       y = "Posterior probability per grid point",
       title = "2 survivors out of 5 seedlings; prior Beta(8,2)")
```

Only the prior changes. The posterior shifts towards higher survival
probabilities; a high-survival prior needs ecological justification.
All these figures show probability per grid point, rather than continuous density.

## Stan demonstration

```{r stan-result}
fit <- course_fit("day1_seedling")
knitr::kable(course_diagnostics(fit),digits=2)
ggplot(as_tibble(fit$draws),aes(p))+geom_histogram(bins=30,fill="#d95f02")+
  labs(x="Survival probability",y="Posterior draws")
```

This is the 2/5, Beta(1,1) posterior. Stored draws approximate a distribution.
